newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Norilsk union says may discuss disrupting output.
newsitem.headline: Norilsk union says may discuss disrupting output.

text.p: Unpaid workers at Russian Norilsk Nickel's financially-troubled main plant will discuss on March 1 the possibility of taking action that could disrupt future output, a senior trade union official said on Monday.

"That question (of disrupting output) will be defined during the March 1 conference, and there is absolutely nothing else on this point that I can tell you, because it is an issue that must be discussed on many levels with many people, and we have not done that," Boris Degtyaryov, deputy head of the plant's United Trade Union committee, said by telephone from Norilsk.

He said that the management of RAO Norilsky Nickel had taken a broad decision to temporarily halt restructuring the main plant, the Norilsk mining and metallurgical combine, but that was not enough to satify disgruntled workers.
"They have fulfilled one of our seven demands -- that the restructuring plan be temporarily halted," Degtyaryov said from the Arctic town.
But he described recent talks with management about repayment of salary arrears, wage increases and improved living conditions as "unsatisfactory".
Some workers had been partially paid their November 1996 salaries, he said, adding that workers and management would meet on March 1 in Norilsk to discuss many issues.
He said that current output was normal.

"We are not opposed to restructuring per se, but it must be done correctly," he said, adding that workers had reacted negatively to the metal group's plan to close nickel processing operations at the main plant and transfer them to other units.
Norilsk shareholder Uneximbank, which controls a 38 percent stake, or 51 percent of voting shares, in the Norilsk group, is struggling to implement a stabilisation package for the company.
Norilsk is a major world producer of nickel, cobalt, platinum, palladium and related metals, as well as of copper.
